title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Sep 2, 2026
summary: EFFIS raised the EU's cumulative 2026 wildfire total to 646,628 hectares as of 1 September, up from 636,100 ha a week earlier and still well above the 20-year seasonal average despite trailing 2025's record pace. Romania's Cernavodă nuclear plant remained fully offline heading into September, with the government's energy-sector state of alert still in force through 30 September and Danube flow forecasts continuing to fluctuate between roughly 1,450 and 1,600 m3/s against a historical August average of 3,900 m3/s. No new acute wildfire outbreaks, fatalities, or evacuations were confirmed in the Aug 27-Sep 2 window across Spain, France, Italy, Portugal, Greece or Romania.

title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Aug 31, 2026
summary: Romania's government extended the energy sector's state of alert by a full month, from 31 August to 30 September 2026, after concluding the Danube's hydrological deficit remains too severe to restart either Cernavodă reactor; officials also cited a weaker wind/solar forecast and rising peak demand. Grid operator Transelectrica and Nuclearelectrica continued leaning on emergency power imports via Ukraine and Moldova's Energocom to cover the shortfall, first activated in early August. EFFIS put the EU's cumulative 2026 wildfire total at 636,100 hectares as of 30 August — still below 2025's record pace but well above the 20-year average — as a heat dome held 40-43°C highs over Italy and the Balkans through the end of the month.

title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Aug 30, 2026
summary: Cernavodă's scheduled Unit 2 outage window expires at midnight with no restart yet confirmed by Nuclearelectrica, as Romania continues building a temporary guide dam on the Old Danube arm and releasing Olt River reservoir water to restore cooling flow. The EU's cumulative 2026 wildfire total holds near 634,500 hectares as the sixth seasonal heat dome continues pushing 40-43°C highs into Italy and the Balkans. Backfilled reporting confirmed Serbia's Deliblato Sands wildfire — burning intermittently since 5 August in a Vojvodina nature reserve east of Belgrade — grew to more than 3,500 hectares and drew EU rescEU helicopters plus a Russian Ilyushin waterbomber before improving by 25 August, with President Vučić touring the site and no casualties reported.

title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Aug 29, 2026
summary: A sixth heat dome of the season pushed into Italy and the Balkans from 27 August, driving temperatures to 42-43°C across the Po Valley, Croatia, Hungary, Serbia and Bosnia and threatening to further delay the Danube's recovery. Romania's Cernavodă nuclear plant remained fully offline as authorities raced to complete a temporary guide dam on the Old Danube arm and continued releasing water from Olt River reservoirs, with flow still holding near a third of the historical average. The EU's cumulative 2026 burned area rose to 634,473 hectares as of 27 August, with the fire-danger map continuing to shift east. Aragón's Peñas de Riglos fire, which killed a UME soldier and forced over 1,000 evacuations, was confirmed stabilized at an 18,400-hectare perimeter after the region's largest-ever firefighting mobilization.

title: Europe Climate Crisis 2026 Update — Aug 21, 2026
summary: Belgium's largest wildfire on record burned roughly 3,000 hectares in the High Fens and pushed smoke toward Germany, while a Spanish UME soldier was killed fighting Aragón's 16,600-hectare Peñas de Riglos fire, which also forced 1,045 evacuations. Greece evacuated 481 people by sea from a Halkidiki blaze, and a second Landes fire near Luglon burned 1,700 hectares before being contained. Romania restarted a 300 MW coal unit at Rovinari and unblocked the long-delayed Bala 2 project to secure future Danube cooling water, as both Cernavodă reactors remained offline. EFFIS put the EU's cumulative 2026 burned area at 619,613 hectares, still below 2025's record pace, while a new Bloomberg tally put Europe-wide heat deaths above 25,000 since April.
